summary: The story is well planted on paper and mostly readable in pictures: the split-screen premise, the F test turning into the A+, the backup sensor shown on the robot (S056/S060) well before the climax, the overhead bump (S077) and recovery from the same spot (S094), and the piano callback. V1 is badly let down by a pipeline bug, though. render.html called buildTimeline(BEATS, window.VO_DUR || {}), but the renderer injects window.VO, so every VO line was timed as a 2.5 s placeholder with speaker 'NAR' (see timeline.json: all lines have dur 2.5 and spk NAR). The mixer then laid the real mp3s (up to 8.4 s long) at those starts. Result: 35 of 80 line pairs overlap, by up to 3.8 s. The narrator talks over himself (L031/L032/L033, L059/L060, L076/L077) and over the characters (L027 over Noah's L028, L035 over the student's L036, L064 over L065, L042 over Eli's L043). Every cut anchored to a line lands at the wrong moment, and no character's mouth ever moves, because speak('ELI'/'NOA'/...) never matches a 'NAR' line. A first-time viewer cannot follow large stretches. (The working tree already has render.html patched to window.VO, uncommitted and after the V1 render, so V2 must be re-rendered. Timings will grow by about 75 s, and every on-screen and VO match needs rechecking.) On the picture side there are many sense errors: dawn followed by a moonlit room, two scoreboards that disagree through the whole final, the announcer's arm drawn across his face, Eli missing from his own Rubik's-cube challenge, a giant screwdriver dropped on the floor instead of set on a bench, the robot passing through the barrier in the payoff shot, floating disembodied arms, foreground shoulders in dialogue shots that face the camera, Eli's 'determined' face reading as anger in the wrong beats, and the final callback face not matching the 'Wait... what?' face.
strengths: Backup sensor is properly planted: the blue box is on the robot in S056 and S060 (labelled BACKUP SENSOR · LEFT SIDE) and in S072/S093/S095/S104; the diagram in S060 says BACKUP / LEFT / METAL CAN CONFUSE IT.
Cause and effect in the climax is mostly right: S077 robot leaves the dotted route and bumps a barrier, S094 resumes from that exact barrier and reaches the finish with 0:03→0:01.
Wardrobe continuity is solid: Eli red hoodie and Noah light-blue shirt + yellow cap in every shot; the cap is absent from the workshop after Noah leaves (S068).
Prop continuity is good on the photo (on Eli's bench from S055 through S068, paid off in S104) and the TEAM: ELI & NOAH card (S071).
Screen geography in the hall shout exchange is consistent: Eli points screen-right toward Noah (S085), Noah points screen-left back (S090).
Strong visual rhymes: the S046 classroom repeat with the same quadratic on the board as S022, the S047 A+ test, the S105 overhead keys with a blue sleeve (Noah) instead of red.

issues.problem: V1 timeline ignored the real VO data: every line has dur 2.5 and spk 'NAR' because render.html passed window.VO_DUR (undefined) instead of window.VO. 35 VO overlaps (up to 3.8 s): narrator lines play on top of each other (L032+L033, L059+L060, L076+L077, L020+L021+L022) and over dialogue (L027 over Noah's 'Bro, since WHEN', L035 over 'Bet you can't solve this', L042 still playing under Eli's 'Already fixed it', L064 under L065). Shot cuts tied to lines with 'on:' therefore happen at the wrong moment, and nobody's mouth moves on dialogue (speak(SPK[who]) never matches).
issues.fix: render.html: buildTimeline(BEATS, window.VO || {}) (already patched in the working tree, so commit it). Re-render, then assert in tools/build.sh that timeline.json lines have varied dur and the correct spk (fail the build if every dur == 2.5). Check that no two lines overlap (start[i+1] >= end[i] - 0.05, except the deliberate L042→L043 interruption, where L042 should be cut with a fade at L043.start in mix.py).

issues.problem: Two contradictory clocks: the arena scoreboard behind the action always reads 'ROUND 1 / 1:00' (sharp in S084 and S090) while the overlay timer counts down 0:28 → 0:17 → 0:09 in the same frames (S079, S080, S085, S089). The scoreboard also still says ROUND 1 during the FINAL and after the win (S097-S102).
issues.fix: act3.js arena(): pass round:'FINAL' and clock: fmtClock(finalClock(c.T)) from one global function of absolute time (the same one S075/S079/S094 use) for every shot from S075 on. After S095 show 'WINNER' and freeze at 0:01. In S074 show 'ROUND 2 ✓'.

issues.problem: Time of day breaks: VO says 'one morning' and S019 shows a 6:00 AM sunrise, but the very next shot and the whole discovery scene (S020, S023, S025, S026, S029) show a dark room with a full moon in the window.
issues.fix: env.js ENV.bedroom: add a tod:'dawn' option (warm low sun instead of the moon disc, pink-orange sky gradient, sun shaft instead of moon shaft). Use bedroomDesk(c,{tod:'dawn'}) for all B08-B12 shots (S020-S029). Keep night for S041-S044 (where 2:00 AM is intended).

issues.problem: The announcer's raised arm is drawn straight up across his own face, which blacks out the face and reads like a pole stuck through his head. No headset is visible, so he is not identifiable as the announcer.
issues.fix: act3.js S074: use the far arm (f:-1 or a 3/4 turn) or a pose with the arm raised out to the side (shoulder abducted about 135°) so the hand clears the head silhouette. Draw the headset mic (character sheet tag) and keep expr 'shout'/'happy' visible.

issues.problem: Eli is not in the shot: the green-cap student slaps the cube on an empty desk and points at nothing. His leg is also drawn over the front of the desk, so he seems to stand on or through it. A viewer cannot tell who he is challenging.
issues.fix: act2.js S051: add Eli seated at the desk on screen-left (back three-quarter, looking up at the student). Put the student behind the desk (draw the desk after his legs, or move him to y = desk back edge) and keep his eyeline on Eli.

issues.problem: Payoff shot ('turned... missed the barrier'): the robot drives straight across the metal barrier box, which is drawn level with and overlapping its roof mid-shot, so it reads as passing through the barrier rather than steering around it. No turn is visible.
issues.fix: act3.js S093: put the barrier in the near lane (lower y, drawn in front of the robot), and have the robot arc away into depth (y up, scale down slightly, yaw 10-15°) before the barrier, then return to the lane after it. Flash the blue LED on just before the swerve so the cause (backup sensor) precedes the effect.

issues.problem: Key emotional beat: Noah holds a screwdriver as long as his torso, like a baton. The 'lowers it to the bench' never happens: there is no bench in frame, and the tool pops to a tiny screwdriver lying at the bottom frame edge, which reads as dropped on the floor. In S067 the screwdriver is gone from both floor and bench.
issues.fix: act3.js S066: scale the screwdriver to hand size (about 0.35 of the current size) and add Noah's bench top in the foreground (y ≈ 900). Animate the hand lowering it slowly to the bench surface and keep it there at the same scale (no swap). S067/S068: draw the screwdriver lying on Noah's empty bench next to the blue tray.

issues.problem: Eli stands facing screen-right with a scowl, watching Noah leave, which contradicts 'Eli didn't notice it at first' (S068 VO) and the shot description 'Eli keeps working'.
issues.fix: act3.js S067: turn Eli to his bench and robot (f toward screen-left, pose sitType/working, head down, expr 'focused') for the whole shot while Noah exits. Have Noah exit through the door (clip him at the door frame instead of popping out).

issues.problem: Blocking contradicts the lines. Noah is supposed to point at his sensor drawing but points at Eli's chest, which reads as an accusation. Eli 'without looking up' instead faces Noah or the camera head-on with an angry scowl and is not working (S061 static for 3 s). The dismissal reads as a fight, not obliviousness.
issues.fix: act3.js: S059 have Noah turn to his bench and point at the diagram (or hold it up). S061/S063/S065 have Eli seated at his bench facing the robot or laptop (profile or back three-quarter), head down, typing pose P.sitType, expr 'focused'/'neutral', speaking over his shoulder. Reserve 'determined' brows for action beats.

issues.problem: The flashback is supposed to match S059/S060 but shows a composition the viewer never saw: a huge diagram floating in mid-air with no easel, Noah alone pointing at it, Eli absent. It is also warm orange rather than the sepia flashback grade, so it is hard to read as memory.
issues.fix: act3.js S087: reuse the exact S059 two-shot framing and props (Eli at left, Noah at right with the diagram on his bench, or the S060 diagram insert), then apply a sepia grade (desaturate + #e8c89a tint + vignette) and the flash-in. Keep the BACKUP · LEFT label legible.

issues.problem: Over-the-shoulder shots show the foreground character's face (eyes and mouth visible, looking at the camera) instead of the back of the head, so the two characters seem not to look at each other and the eyeline is broken.
issues.fix: In these shots render the foreground actor with a back/three-quarter-back option (no face features, hood or cap seen from behind) facing the speaker. Turn the speaker's head 15-20° toward the foreground shoulder (S017 Noah looks screen-left, S018 Eli looks screen-right, and so on).

issues.problem: The trophy floats in mid-air in the foreground with no one holding it and no stand (the shot description says 'held up'). Eli looks at the camera, not past the trophy toward Noah.
issues.fix: act3.js S097: add an official's arm/hand (sleeve running off-frame) gripping the trophy, or a podium under it. Turn Eli's head and eyes screen-right toward where Noah sits (consistent with S090).

issues.problem: The red-sleeved arm floats with its sleeve ending in mid-frame (no shoulder, not entering from the edge). At the end of the shot the F stamp shrinks to a tiny unreadable green dot, and the sheet still shows 2 red crosses, so the 'grade becomes 9/10' beat never reads.
issues.fix: act1.js S027: lengthen the sleeve so it enters from the bottom-right frame edge. End on 6/7 ticks and replace the F with a full-size green stamp reading '6/7' (same 1:1 size as the F), popping in with the success chime.

issues.problem: Disembodied limbs: in S056 Eli's red arm and Noah's blue arm float in mid-air with sleeve ends inside the frame, and the S091 thumb arm does the same. In the hand inserts the hands are flat open palms hovering above the keys with fingers pointing up.
issues.fix: Extend every insert arm so the sleeve continues past the nearest frame edge (start point at least 150 px outside the frame). In piano/keyboard inserts rotate the hands to palms down with fingertips on the keys (fingers pointing away from camera).

issues.problem: Desk scale/placement is wrong: Eli sits with his head at desk-top height, so the open book floats above his head. In S044 'asleep on his textbook' his head is under the book, not on it.
issues.fix: act1.js bedroomDesk(): raise Eli and the stool by about 120 px (or lower the desk top) so his elbows rest on the desk surface and the book sits in front of his chest. In S044 put his head on the open book (head y = desk top − head radius).

issues.problem: The callback does not match: the 'Wait... what?' face in S026 is wide shock eyes with an O mouth, while S108 uses the half-lidded 'bewildered' face, so the 'same look' callback doesn't read. The end title is also composited over Eli's face, so the text crosses his eyes.
issues.fix: act1.js S026: use expr 'bewildered' (per the character sheet) with the same framing and scale as S108 (headAt and h identical). act3.js S108: fade Eli out (or push him to the left third) before the title fades in, or move the title to the lower third.

issues.problem: Seating continuity: in S106 both boys end up seated at the piano, but in S107 Noah is standing and walking and in S108 Eli is standing. Eli also 'sits down' by hopping into the air and landing on the stool (one frame shows him floating above it).
issues.fix: act3.js S107/S108: use seated poses (P.sit) with the piano edge in frame. In S106 replace the hop with a walk-in, turn, and lower-hips sit over about 0.6 s with the feet staying on the floor.

issues.problem: The teacher's identity tag (round white-rim glasses) disappears: the shock eyes replace the glasses, so 'glasses slide down in surprise' is not shown and he reads as a random grey adult.
issues.fix: rig.js: draw the teacher's glasses as a separate layer independent of expr. In S048 animate the glasses sliding down 25 px over 0.4 s, with the shock eyes visible above the rims.

issues.problem: Eli's 'determined' face (sharp inward brows) reads as anger in beats that need other emotions. In S050 he scowls at friends offering GUITAR?/CHESS? (should be hungry/eager), and in S098 he marches to apologise with an angry face (should be sincere/remorseful).
issues.fix: Use expr 'happy'/'focused' in S050 (eager grin), 'worried'/'sad' in S098, and 'focused' in S071. Reduce the brow angle of 'determined' in rig.js by about 40% so it reads as resolve, not rage.

issues.problem: Text overlaps text on the key clue diagram: the grey 'METAL' tag sits on top of the red 'METAL CAN CONFUSE IT!' line, hiding 'CON'.
issues.fix: Move the METAL tag up to the barrier line (y − 40) or move the red caption 50 px below the line.

issues.problem: Eli lands head-first (head at the ground, legs up in a diagonal) and freezes in that pose for about 1.7 s. It reads as a stuck frame rather than 'falls on his back', and the ball barely rolls.
issues.fix: act1.js S013: end the fall flat on his back (torso horizontal at ground y, legs slightly raised), add a small bounce/settle and blink, and roll the ball 300+ px toward the goal with ease-out.

issues.problem: The friends 'point at a guitar, hoop poster, chess flyer' but no objects exist, only floating words. The third word ('RUBIK'S CUBE?') is washed out over the bright doorway and unreadable, and it pre-empts the S051 reveal.
issues.fix: act2.js S050: draw small props (guitar on a locker, chess flyer, hoop poster) with each friend pointing at one and the label under the prop. Drop the cube label.

issues.problem: Side views put the blue backup box on the robot's rear end (labelled 'LEFT SIDE'), while top views show it on the robot's left flank. This is a small geometry inconsistency in the key clue.
issues.fix: Mount the blue box on the rear-left corner in both the props.js robot side view and the top view so 'left' is true from every angle, or relabel the side-view callout 'BACKUP (left side)' with an arrow to a box peeking over the far side.
